plan_summary: The vulnerability assessment will proceed in phases: initial information gathering, automated scanning for known vulnerabilities, manual review of critical configurations (e.g., SSH, services), and finally, compiling a prioritized, actionable remediation plan.
assumptions: The user has root or equivalent administrative access to the Linux host.
The host is operational and accessible for scanning.
The scope of the assessment is limited to the local host and its installed software/configurations.

tasks.title: System Information Gathering
tasks.objective: Collect baseline data on the operating system, kernel version, installed packages, and network configuration.
tasks.rationale: Understanding the current state is necessary to scope the assessment and identify potential outdated components.
tasks.expected_output: Comprehensive report detailing OS version, kernel version, installed package list (e.g., dpkg -l or rpm -qa), and network interfaces.
success_criteria: A list of all major installed packages is generated.

tasks.title: Automated Vulnerability Scanning
tasks.objective: Run industry-standard tools (e.g., OpenVAS, Nessus, or local package vulnerability checkers) to identify known Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs).
tasks.rationale: Automated scanning provides a broad, systematic check against known security flaws in installed software.
inputs_required: Network connectivity (if external scanning is required)
tasks.expected_output: A list of identified vulnerabilities, including CVE IDs, affected packages, and severity ratings.
success_criteria: All major installed services are scanned.
A report detailing high and medium severity CVEs is generated.

tasks.title: Configuration Hardening Review (SSH/Services)
tasks.objective: Manually review critical configuration files (e.g., /etc/ssh/sshd_config, firewall rules, service unit files) for insecure defaults or weak settings.
tasks.rationale: Automated scanners often miss misconfigurations. This step focuses on common human-error vulnerabilities.
inputs_required: System configuration files (e.g., sshd_config, iptables rules)
tasks.expected_output: A list of insecure configurations (e.g., password authentication enabled, weak ciphers, unnecessary services running).
success_criteria: SSH configuration is reviewed for best practices (e.g., key-only auth, disabling root login).
Firewall rules are checked for overly permissive ingress/egress rules.

tasks.title: User and Access Control Review
tasks.objective: Audit user accounts, group memberships, and sudo privileges to ensure the principle of least privilege is maintained.
tasks.rationale: Excessive user permissions are a common attack vector. This task ensures only necessary access is granted.
tasks.expected_output: Report detailing users with excessive privileges or inactive accounts that should be removed/restricted.
success_criteria: All non-essential user accounts are identified.
Sudo privileges are restricted to specific commands rather than full root access.

tasks.title: Remediation Plan Generation
tasks.objective: Synthesize findings from T02, T03, and T04 into a prioritized, actionable remediation plan.
tasks.rationale: The goal is not just to find flaws, but to provide clear, step-by-step instructions for fixing them.
tasks.expected_output: A prioritized remediation plan categorized by severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low) with specific commands or configuration changes.
success_criteria: Every identified vulnerability or misconfiguration has a corresponding remediation step.
The plan is ordered by impact and ease of implementation.
